chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Salih ibn 'Uqba from Abu Harun al-Makfuuf who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Harun, the Iqamah is part of the Salat. So when you call the Iqamah, do not speak and do not gesture with your hand.'

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited immediately before standing for prayer.
key_terms.تُومِ: Gesture: To move the hand or body to signal or indicate.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking or gesturing during the Iqamah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Iqamah from a mere announcement to an intrinsic component of the prayer ritual itself. He specifically commands silence and stillness during its recitation, prohibiting speech and hand gestures to ensure the congregation remains in a state of focused reverence (khushu) as the transition to the standing position occurs.
